voyage.name: Faro Voltiano
voyage.content: 29-m tower was erected in 1927 in honour of Alessandro Volta. Boasting some of the best views on the lake, this very high building will allow you to look down on the lake some 2000 feet below. The views are much better than from the free terrace below.

voyage.name: Cattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta
voyage.content: Como's richly decorated 14th-century Gothic-Renaissance Cathedral. Note the statues of Pliny the Elder and Younger at the sides of the main entrance!

voyage.name: Basilica di Sant'Abbondio
voyage.content: A Romanesque basilica built in 11th century; inside some 13th-century frescos. The basilica was built on the site of an early Christian basilica of the 5th century, dedicated to the holy apostles Peter and Paul. Between 1050 and 1095, the Benedictines rebuilt the church in Romanesque style. voyage.name: Tempio Voltiano
voyage.content: A nice stop on your stroll along the waterfront, the temple to Volta is designed in neoclassical style. It houses an exhibition about Volta (a native of Como who invented the electric battery). The front of the building showcases two statues, representing science and faith. It was featured on the Italian 10,000-lira note before the introduction of the euro.

voyage.name: War Memorial
voyage.content: An interesting, imposing, 33-m-high building, it is one of the tallest structures near the water. Built in the 1930s to honour Italian soldiers killed in World War I.

voyage.name: City Walls
voyage.content: The ruins of the 12th-century city walls, which encircle the narrow, winding streets of the old town. The old town is still called the "walled town" (città murata).

voyage.name: Museo Archeologico Paolo Giovio
voyage.content: Museum showing the history of Como - also features Egyptian and Greek artefacts.

voyage.name: Museo Storico Giuseppe Garibaldi
voyage.content: Opened in 1932, another museum featuring Como's history.

voyage.name: Pinacoteca Civica
voyage.content: The building was constructed in the 17th century, and has been an art gallery since the 1980s. It exhibits sculptures, portraits, and tapestries by famous artists.

voyage.name: Fontana di Villa Geno
voyage.content: Large fountain that - when switched on - can be seen from Como. Worth a walk along the edge of the lake to see it, however, it may not always be on.

voyage.name: Villa Olmo
voyage.content: Built in the early 19th century, this is an impressive, ornate palace, owned by the town of Como. The lakefront gardens are open to the public. The building is open to the public to visit the beautifully decorated but unfurnished rooms, except during special events. The park of Villa Olmo is certainly one of the most important in the entire province of Como. Since its origins, the land extends for almost five hectare

voyage.name: Walk along the waterfront
voyage.content: Como has a pleasant walkway along the water. It passes by the Tempio Voltiano, the World War I memorial, and several beautiful villas. The path is also pleasantly dotted with gellaterias - you can walk as far as the Villa Olmo to the west and the Fontana di Villa Geno to the east quite easily, which on a sunny day would give great views over the lake.

voyage.name: Bicycle ride
voyage.content: Rent a bicycle and ride up the hill into Switzerland before descending over the other side to the beautiful Lake Lugano. Follow the lake north to the Swiss city of Lugano. Head east from Lugano and back across the border into Italy. When you reach Lake Como, turn south and return to the city of Como, completing the circle. Or you could do as the locals do, and use a bike to explore the city of Como itself.

voyage.name: Hike in the mountains
voyage.content: Take the funicular up to Brunate, then (after seeing the Faro Voltiano) hike through the nearby mountains for great views of the area. See the signs and maps at the top of the funicular for routes, but remember to bring a lot of water in summer, as it can get very warm and sunny.

voyage.name: Centro Sportivo Casate
voyage.content: Sports centre, with swimming pools (including an outdoor one), volleyball courts, etc. It has activities on in the winter too, including ice skating.

voyage.name: Piscina Sinigaglia
voyage.content: The town's indoor swimming pool, next to the football stadium, good if you want to swim lengths - if you want outdoor swimming however, go to the lido.

voyage.name: Lido Villa Olmo
voyage.price: €5.50 for an afternoon; €8.50 for a whole day.
voyage.content: Lido on the edge of Lake Como just next to Villa Olmo - gives travellers the chance to swim in the lake, which is very tempting on hot summer days. The lido also features a bar, and entrance can be pre-booked online at their website.

voyage.name: Como 1907
voyage.content: "I Lariani" were promoted in 2024 and now play soccer in Serie A, the top tier. B. With a capacity of 13,600, Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia is too cramped for top tier matches: it hasn't been announced whether it will be upgraded or if Como will play elsewhere. Sinigaglia (1884-1916) was a champion rower, killed in action in the war with Austria.

voyage.name: Fly in a seaplane
voyage.content: If you are in Como, you'll quickly notice the regular seaplane flights over the lake. Aero Club Como offer private seaplane flights for visitors, as well as pilot training. Even if you don't actually book a flight, it's well worth passing by the hangar to have a look at the sea planes.

voyage.name: Horseriding
voyage.content: Take a ride on horseback in the Parco Pineta di Appiano e Tradate. From Limido Comasco, 25 minutes drive from Como. English and western style riding in beautiful woodlands with friendly English/French and Italian speaking guides. Local Centered Riding instructor available for private lessons.

voyage.name: Panino Buono
voyage.content: Italian style sandwiches, a common lunch option for people who work nearby.

voyage.name: La pizzaccia
voyage.content: Mid-priced pizza and an excellent selection of beers.

voyage.name: Birreria
voyage.content: Relax in the bohemian and friendly atmosphere of this pub, where you can sit down at the wooden tables and enjoy beer (and any other drinks) and snacks. The walls are covered with all sorts of objects from around the world, musical instruments, paintings, photos etc. You are likely to hear Bob Dylan, Simon & Garfunkel or Fabrizio de Andrè (Italian singer/songwriter) playing on the Hi-Fi system.

A cozy bar that is a meeting place for local arty people, different from the Italian fashion victims clique. Highly recommended starting from 19:00 on Sundays for aperitivo (buffet food with any drinks purchased).

voyage.name: La Pinta di Volta
voyage.address: at the end of lungolago Mafalda di Savoia
voyage.content: A small chiringuito (small bar) on an amazing location just in front of tempio voltiano. Superb lake view, great choice of cocktails as well as nice aperitivo.

voyage.name: 125 Pizzeria
voyage.content: A small pizzeria, really good for aperitivo. Live concert every Friday evening.

voyage.name: B&B Dolce Lario
voyage.content: A few kilometres from the historical centre and very close to the stations and main road.

voyage.name: Respau Eco Hostel
voyage.address: Via Santa Brigida e Respau, Cascina Respau di Sotto
voyage.content: Located in the heart of the Spina Verde Natural Park, a few minutes bus ride from the city centre.

voyage.name: Tornoalago
voyage.content: Flats, studios and villas in Torno, in a truly romantic spot on Lake Como.

voyage.name: Hotel delle Fiere
voyage.address: Via Trieste and Via Piccinelli, Mozzate
voyage.content: 4-star wellness hotel in Mozzate, between Como and Milan.

voyage.name: Hotel Plinius
voyage.content: 3-star hotel in Como centre.

voyage.name: Villa d'Este
voyage.content: Villa d'Este used to be the residence of the Cardinal Tolomeo Gallio and nowadays it's a luxury hotel.
